description: cjson.decode nil invokes fallback, then falls through and indexes response_json.version/content.
cjson.decode is unprotected; an exception or truthy non-table result aborts/errors before format fallback can complete.
Failed backup requests with force_refresh=false can resubmit without an explicit retry cap, delay, or backoff.
write_file returns on a nil write result without closing the already-open file handle.
Statements can follow core_func_exit/core_func_byby; safe control flow assumes those host APIs never return (the backup kill token path has no explicit return).
The pcall success flag key_derivation_ok is ignored before core_archive_key is concatenated and used.
Non-200 HTTP responses return silently without retry or fallback in that callback.
Cache write return values are ignored and files are replaced directly rather than atomically, allowing stale/partial cache state.
Core archive decrypt/write/ZIP-load/remove results are not validated; optional hookcore ZIP is loaded without a visible authenticity check.
gplus MD5, UUID reads/writes, gate IP, and crypto return values are concatenated without comprehensive nil/type validation.
When bzuuid is absent, the identifier seed is only os.time() at second precision before MD5, so it is predictable and collision-prone.
Plain-HTTP responses are decrypted and executed through load/pcall, and hookcore ZIP can be loaded, with no separate signature/authenticity verification visible in Lua.
POST bodies are manually concatenated without visible percent-encoding; Base64 and other field characters may depend on host API/server parsing behavior.
Some getinfo checks inspect a related API while execution uses a wrapper or object method, so the exact invoked implementation is not always the checked object.
A fixed server response token invokes core_func_exit in all three network callback families.
Execution depends on LuaJIT/Lua 5.1 behavior and many nonstandard game-host globals/APIs; the source is not a standalone Lua program.
